lessons.title: Reference: the 16-week day-by-day plan
lessons.description: Sixteen weeks, five study days a week, with every module placed on a day.
lessons.content:
## How to use this plan

Sixteen weeks, five study days a week, roughly two hours a day. That is eight to
ten hours a week including the labs and assignments.

The course is self-paced. This plan exists for people who want one, not because
the dates matter. Two days a week are deliberately left free: use them to catch
up, or do not use them at all.

**The weekly rhythm is the same every week:**

```
  Day 1   teaching lessons        learn the concepts
  Day 2   teaching lessons        learn the concepts
  Day 3   teaching lessons        finish the module's teaching
  Day 4   practice + lab          40 questions, then build something
  Day 5   assignment + assessment produce the deliverable, then test yourself
  Day 6   free                    catch up, or rest
  Day 7   free                    rest
```

If you fall behind, drop the catch-up days before you drop the labs. The labs
are where the learning actually happens.

---

## Level 1 — Beginner (weeks 1 to 6)

### Week 1 — Digital Marketing Fundamentals (module 1)

| Day | What you do |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | What digital marketing is · traditional vs digital · the ecosystem |
| 2 | Customer journey and funnel · B2B and B2C |
| 3 | Target audience and personas · segmentation · objectives and KPIs · how a strategy fits together |
| 4 | Practice questions (40) · lab: persona, funnel and KPIs for Petal & Pine |
| 5 | Assignment: one-page marketing brief · assessment |

### Week 2 — Website and Landing Pages (module 2)

| Day | What you do |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Website structure · domains and hosting · UX and UI basics |
| 2 | Landing pages · CTA design · lead-generation forms |
| 3 | Conversion basics · WordPress basics · Analytics and Search Console setup |
| 4 | Practice questions · lab: build a landing page in HTML and CSS |
| 5 | Assignment: a landing page for Bright Mile Dental · assessment |

### Week 3 — SEO foundations (module 3, first half)

| Day | What you do |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | What SEO is · how search engines work · crawling, indexing and ranking |
| 2 | Keyword research · search intent |
| 3 | On-page SEO · off-page SEO |
| 4 | Re-read anything from days 1 to 3 that did not land |
| 5 | Free: SEO is the longest module, so this day is slack by design |

### Week 4 — SEO in depth (module 3, second half)

| Day | What you do |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Technical SEO · Core Web Vitals · local SEO · international SEO |
| 2 | Link building · internal linking · SEO content strategy |
| 3 | Structured data and schema · SEO audits · competitor analysis · the toolkit |
| 4 | Practice questions · lab: an SEO audit and keyword strategy |
| 5 | Assignment: an SEO audit report for Craftwise Academy · assessment |

### Week 5 — Content Marketing (module 4)

| Day | What you do |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | What content marketing is · content strategy · content pillars |
| 2 | Blog strategy · content calendar · copywriting fundamentals |
| 3 | Storytelling · headlines and hooks · lead magnets · e-books · distribution · repurposing · AI-assisted content |
| 4 | Practice questions · lab: a 30-day content calendar |
| 5 | Assignment: a content plan for Shiftly · assessment |

### Week 6 — Social Media Marketing (module 5)

| Day | What you do |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Social media strategy · Facebook · Instagram · LinkedIn |
| 2 | YouTube as a social channel · X · short-form video · Reels and Shorts |
| 3 | Community · hashtags · calendar · engagement · influencers · analytics |
| 4 | Practice questions · lab: a social media strategy for a brand |
| 5 | Assignment: a 30-day social plan for Petal & Pine · assessment |

**End of Level 1.** Sit the Level 1 exam before you move on.

---

## Level 2 — Intermediate (weeks 7 to 12)

| 4 | Practice questions · lab: build a Google Search Ads campaign |
| 5 | Assignment: a Google Ads plan for Bright Mile Dental · assessment |

### Week 9 — YouTube Marketing (module 8)

### Week 10 — Email Marketing (module 9)

### Week 12 — Analytics and Measurement (module 11)

---

## Level 3 — Advanced (weeks 13 to 15)

Two modules a week from here. The days are fuller; use the catch-up days.

### Week 13 — CRO and Influencer/Affiliate (modules 12 and 13)

| Day | What you do |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Module 12: what CRO is · conversion funnel · landing page, CTA and form optimisation |
| 2 | Module 12: A/B testing · heatmaps · user behaviour · experiments · practice · lab |
| 3 | Module 12 assignment and assessment · start module 13 |
| 4 | Module 13: influencers, types, selection, planning, negotiation, measurement, affiliates · practice · lab |
| 5 | Module 13 assignment and assessment |

### Week 14 — E-commerce and AI in Marketing (modules 14 and 15)

| Day | What you do |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Module 14: funnel · product pages · product SEO · Shopping · Meta commerce |
| 2 | Module 14: retargeting · cart recovery · reviews · upselling · marketplaces · retention · practice · lab |
| 3 | Module 14 assignment and assessment · start module 15 |
| 4 | Module 15: AI for content, images, video, social, SEO, research, analytics, chatbots, automation, prompting, agents · practice · lab |
| 5 | Module 15 assignment and assessment |

### Week 15 — AI Search and Automation (modules 16 and 17)

| Day | What you do |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Module 16: SEO vs AEO vs GEO · AEO · GEO · AI search · intent |
| 2 | Module 16: entities · structured content · knowledge graphs · mentions · measuring AI visibility · practice · lab |
| 3 | Module 16 assignment and assessment · start module 17 |
| 4 | Module 17: automation, lead scoring, nurture, CRM, workflows, webhooks, the toolkit · practice · lab |
| 5 | Module 17 assignment and assessment |

**End of Level 3.** Sit the Level 3 exam before you move on.

---

## Levels 4 and 5 (week 16 and beyond)

### Week 16 — Strategy and Career (modules 18 and 19)

| Day | What you do |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Module 18: market research · competitors · SWOT · STP · journey mapping |
| 2 | Module 18: channels · content · paid and organic · budget · planning · KPIs · attribution · ROI · practice · lab |
| 3 | Module 18 assignment and assessment |
| 4 | Module 19: career paths, the six roles, freelancing platforms, finding clients |
| 5 | Module 19: proposals · pricing · communication · reporting · portfolio · LinkedIn · practice · lab · assignment |

**End of Level 4.** Sit the Level 4 exam.

### The capstone (module 20)

The capstone is not a week. It is a project, and it takes as long as it takes —
most people spend two to four weeks on it alongside nothing else.

Do not start it until modules 1 to 19 are done. It reuses every one of them, and
starting early means redoing the early deliverables.

| Stage | What you produce |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Brand choice, market research, buyer persona, competitor analysis |
| 2 | Landing page, keyword research, SEO strategy, content strategy |
| 3 | Social calendar, Meta Ads campaign, Google Ads campaign, email campaign |
| 4 | Analytics setup, dashboard, campaign budget |
| 5 | KPI and ROI report, final presentation |

**End of Level 5.**

## If you have less time

Twelve weeks instead of sixteen: merge weeks 3 and 4 into one SEO week, and
double up weeks 7 to 12 the way weeks 13 to 15 already are. You lose the slack,
not the content.

Nothing in the course expects you to have done it in any particular number of
weeks.

lessons.title: Reference: glossary of digital marketing terms
lessons.description: Over 150 terms defined in one or two sentences, with the module that covers each.
lessons.content:
## How to use this

Every term the course uses, defined in one or two sentences. If a lesson uses a
word you have not met, it is here.

Terms are grouped alphabetically. Where a term is explained properly in a
module, the module number is given.

---

### A

**A/B test** — Showing two versions of one thing to similar audiences, changing
only one variable, to see which performs better. Modules 6 and 12.

**Above the fold** — The part of a page visible before scrolling.

**Ad asset (ad extension)** — Extra information attached to a search ad, such as
site links or a phone number. Module 7.

**Ad creative** — The image, video or text that makes up an advert. Module 6.

**Ad rank** — The score a search engine uses to decide which ads appear and in
what order. Bid is only part of it; relevance matters too. Module 7.

**Advocacy** — The funnel stage where a customer recommends you to someone else.
Module 1.

**AEO (Answer Engine Optimisation)** — Optimising so your content is used as the
answer an engine gives, not only ranked in a list of links. Module 16.

**Affiliate marketing** — Paying a partner a commission for sales they refer.
Module 13.

**Affiliate network** — A platform that connects merchants with affiliates and
handles tracking and payment. Module 13.

**AI search** — Search experiences that return a generated answer rather than
only a list of links. Module 16.

**Algorithm** — The set of rules a platform uses to decide what to show someone.
Nobody outside the platform knows them exactly.

**Alt text** — A text description of an image, used by screen readers and by
search engines. Module 3.

**Attribution** — Deciding which marketing touchpoint gets credit for a
conversion. Module 11.

**Audience** — The group of people you are trying to reach. Module 1.

**Automation** — Making a marketing action happen without someone triggering it
by hand. Module 17.

**Average order value (AOV)** — Total revenue divided by number of orders.
Module 14.

**Awareness** — The funnel stage where someone learns you exist. Module 1.

### B

**B2B** — Business to business: selling to an organisation. Module 1.

**B2C** — Business to consumer: selling to a person buying for themselves.
Module 1.

**Backlink** — A link from another website to yours. Module 3.

**Bid** — What you are willing to pay for a click, an impression or a
conversion. Modules 6 and 7.

**Bidding strategy** — The rule that decides your bid automatically, such as
maximising clicks or hitting a target cost per action. Module 7.

**Bounce rate** — The share of sessions where someone arrived and left without
meaningful interaction. Definitions differ between tools, so check what yours
counts. Module 11.

**Brand mention** — Your brand named somewhere online, with or without a link.
Module 16.

**Broad match** — A keyword match type where the engine shows your ad for
loosely related searches. Module 7.

**Buyer persona** — A short written description of one typical buyer, used to
make decisions. Module 1.

### C

**CAC (Customer Acquisition Cost)** — Total cost of winning a customer: spend
divided by customers won. Module 11.

**Call to action (CTA)** — The specific thing you are asking someone to do, and
the button or link that does it. Module 2.

**Campaign** — A set of marketing activity with one objective, a start and an
end.

**Canonical tag** — Markup telling search engines which version of a duplicated
page is the real one. Module 3.

**Chatbot** — An automated conversational agent that answers questions or
collects details. Module 10.

**Churn** — The rate at which customers stop buying or subscribing. Module 14.

**Click-through rate (CTR)** — Clicks divided by impressions, as a percentage.

**Cohort analysis** — Grouping people by when they joined, then comparing how
each group behaves over time. Module 11.

**Commission model** — How an affiliate is paid: per sale, per lead, or a
revenue share. Module 13.

**Consideration** — The funnel stage where someone compares you with
alternatives. Module 1.

**Content calendar** — A schedule of what will be published, where and when.
Module 4.

**Content pillar** — One of a small set of themes every piece of content ties
back to. Module 4.

**Content repurposing** — Turning one piece of content into several formats for
different channels. Module 4.

**Conversion** — The action you wanted someone to take: a purchase, a booking, a
sign-up. Module 1.

**Conversion funnel** — The sequence of steps between arriving and converting,
used to find where people drop out. Module 12.

**Conversion rate** — Conversions divided by visitors or sessions, as a
percentage.

**Conversion tracking** — The setup that records a conversion and ties it back
to the campaign that caused it. Modules 6, 7 and 11.

**Cookie** — A small file a site stores in a browser, historically used for
tracking. What browsers permit changes often; check current behaviour.

**Core Web Vitals** — A set of page experience measurements covering loading,
interactivity and visual stability. Module 3.

**Cost per click (CPC)** — What you pay for one click.

**Cost per acquisition (CPA)** — What you pay for one conversion.

**Cost per mille (CPM)** — What you pay for a thousand impressions.

**Crawling** — A search engine fetching a page so it can consider it. Module 3.

**CRM (Customer Relationship Management)** — A system holding your contacts,
their history and where they are in the sales process. Module 17.

**CRO (Conversion Rate Optimisation)** — Getting more results from the traffic
you already have, by testing. Module 12.

**Custom audience** — An audience built from your own data, such as a customer
list or site visitors. Module 6.

**Customer journey** — The path from not knowing you exist to buying, and
beyond. Module 1.

**Customer lifetime value (LTV)** — The total profit a customer produces over
the whole relationship. Module 11.

### D

**Dashboard** — A single view of the few numbers that matter, built so someone
can act on it. Module 11.

**Deliverability** — Whether your email reaches the inbox rather than spam or
nowhere. Module 9.

**Demographic segmentation** — Splitting an audience by age, gender, income, job
title or company size. Module 1.

**Display campaign** — Image adverts shown across a network of websites and
apps. Module 7.

**Domain** — The address people type to reach your site. Module 2.

**Drip campaign** — A fixed sequence of emails sent on a schedule after a
trigger. Module 9.

**Dwell time** — How long someone stays on a page after clicking through to it.

### E

**Earned media** — Attention others give you: rankings, reviews, coverage,
recommendations. Module 1.

**E-commerce funnel** — The funnel for selling a product online, from discovery
to repeat purchase. Module 14.

**Email list** — The contacts who have agreed to hear from you. Owned media.
Module 9.

**Engagement rate** — How much an audience interacts with content, relative to
how many saw it. Each platform defines it differently.

**Entity** — A thing a search engine understands as a distinct concept: a
person, a place, a brand. Module 16.

**Evergreen content** — Content that stays useful long after publication.
Module 4.

**Exact match** — A keyword match type restricting ads to searches very close to
your keyword. Module 7.

### F

**Featured snippet** — An answer extracted onto the results page above or among
the normal results. Module 16.

**Form optimisation** — Reducing friction in a form so more people finish it.
Module 12.

**Frequency** — How many times, on average, one person saw your advert.

**Funnel** — The model describing the stages from awareness to advocacy, and
what message each needs. Module 1.

### G

**GEO (Generative Engine Optimisation)** — Optimising to be cited and used
inside AI-generated answers. Module 16.

**Geographic segmentation** — Splitting an audience by country, city or distance
from a location. Module 1.

**Google Business Profile** — A business listing that can appear in local
results and maps. Its features change often; check the current interface.
Module 3.

### H

**Hashtag** — A keyword marked with # used to categorise social posts.
Module 5.

**Heatmap** — A visual summary of where people click, move or scroll on a page.
Module 12.

**Hero section** — The top area of a page carrying the headline and main call to
action. Module 2.

**Hreflang** — Markup telling search engines which language and region a page is
for. Module 3.

### I

**Impression** — One instance of your content or advert being shown.

**Inbound marketing** — Attracting people with useful content rather than
interrupting them.

**Indexing** — A search engine storing a crawled page so it can be returned in
results. Module 3.

**Influencer** — Someone with an audience who can recommend you to it.
Modules 5 and 13.

**Internal link** — A link from one page of your site to another. Module 3.

### J

**Journey map** — A document showing each stage of the customer journey and what
the business does at it. Module 18.

### K

**Keyword** — A word or phrase people type into a search engine. Module 3.

**Keyword difficulty** — An estimate of how hard it would be to rank for a
keyword. Each tool calculates it differently, so the numbers are not
comparable between tools. Module 3.

**Keyword match type** — The rule controlling how closely a search must match
your keyword for the ad to show. Module 7.

**Knowledge graph** — A structured store of entities and the relationships
between them, used to answer questions. Module 16.

**KPI (Key Performance Indicator)** — One of the few metrics you have decided
actually matters for an objective. Module 1.

### L

**Lagging indicator** — A number that reports what already happened, such as
revenue. Module 1.

**Landing page** — A page built to get one specific action from one specific
audience. Module 2.

**Lead** — Someone who has shown interest and can be contacted. Module 1.

**Lead magnet** — Something useful given in exchange for contact details.
Modules 4 and 9.

**Lead nurturing** — Staying useful to a lead until they are ready to buy.
Modules 10 and 17.

**Lead scoring** — Ranking leads by how likely they are to buy, so effort goes
to the best ones. Module 17.

**Leading indicator** — A number that moves early and predicts a later result.
Module 1.

**Link building** — Earning links from other sites to yours. Module 3.

**Local SEO** — Optimising to appear for searches with local intent. Module 3.

**Lookalike audience** — A new audience a platform builds to resemble a source
audience you supply. Module 6.

### M

**Marketing automation** — Software that runs marketing sequences based on
triggers and rules. Module 17.

**Marketing qualified lead (MQL)** — A lead judged ready to be passed to sales.
Module 17.

**Meta description** — The summary text a search engine may show under your
title. Module 3.

**Meta Pixel** — A tracking snippet placed on a site to record actions for ad
measurement and audiences. Module 6.

**Micro-influencer** — A creator with a small but closely engaged audience.
Module 13.

**Mobile-first indexing** — Search engines evaluating the mobile version of a
page as the primary one. Module 3.

### N

**Negative keyword** — A term that stops your ad showing when it appears in a
search. Module 7.

**Newsletter** — A regular email sent to a list. Module 9.

**Nofollow** — A link attribute signalling that a link should not pass ranking
credit. Module 3.

**Nurture sequence** — A planned series of messages that moves a lead towards a
decision. Module 17.

### O

**Off-page SEO** — Work done outside your site that affects how it ranks, mainly
links and mentions. Module 3.

**On-page SEO** — Work done on the page itself: titles, headings, content,
internal links. Module 3.

**Open rate** — The share of delivered emails recorded as opened. Privacy
features affect how reliable this is; treat it as directional. Module 9.

**Organic traffic** — Visitors who arrive without you paying for the click.

**Owned media** — Channels you control: your site, your email list, your
messaging list. Module 1.

### P

**Page speed** — How quickly a page loads and becomes usable. Module 3.

**Paid media** — Attention you rent: ads and sponsorships. Module 1.

**Pay-per-click (PPC)** — Advertising where you pay when someone clicks.
Module 7.

**Performance Max** — A Google campaign type that serves across several
inventories from one campaign. Its controls change often; check the current
interface. Module 7.

**Personalisation** — Changing a message based on what you know about the
recipient. Module 9.

**Pixel** — A tracking snippet on a website that reports visitor actions back to
an ad platform. Module 6.

**Positioning** — What you stand for in the mind of a specific audience, and how
you differ from alternatives. Module 18.

**Psychographic segmentation** — Splitting an audience by attitude and
motivation rather than by who they are. Module 1.

### Q

**Qualified lead** — A lead that matches who you can actually serve.
Module 17.

**Quality Score** — A search engine's estimate of the relevance of your keyword,
ad and landing page. Module 7.

**Query** — What someone actually typed, as opposed to the keyword you bid on.
Module 3.

### R

**Reach** — The number of distinct people who saw something.

**Referral traffic** — Visitors arriving from a link on another site.
Module 11.

**Remarketing / retargeting** — Advertising to people who have already
interacted with you. Modules 6, 7 and 14.

**Retention** — Keeping customers and getting them to buy again. Modules 1
and 14.

**Return on ad spend (ROAS)** — Revenue from advertising divided by the cost of
that advertising. Module 11.

**Return on investment (ROI)** — Profit relative to total cost, usually as a
percentage. Module 11.

**Rich result** — A search result enhanced with extra detail drawn from
structured data. Module 3.

**Robots.txt** — A file telling crawlers which parts of a site they may fetch.
Module 3.

### S

**Schema markup** — Structured data added to a page so machines can understand
what it describes. Module 3.

**Search intent** — What someone actually wants when they type a query:
information, a specific site, a comparison, or to buy. Modules 3 and 16.

**Segment** — A group you can select in a tool and send something different to.
Module 1.

**SERP (Search Engine Results Page)** — The page of results returned for a
query. Module 3.

**Session** — One visit: a set of interactions by one person within a time
window. Module 11.

**Shopping campaign** — Ads showing a product image, title and price, driven by
a product feed. Module 7.

**Sitemap** — A file listing the pages you want search engines to find.
Module 3.

**Social proof** — Evidence that other people chose you: reviews, counts,
testimonials, logos. Module 14.

**STP** — Segmentation, targeting and positioning: who exists, who you choose,
and what you stand for to them. Module 18.

**Structured data** — Machine-readable markup describing a page's contents.
Module 3.

**SWOT** — Strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats. Module 18.

### T

**Target audience** — The group you are trying to reach. Module 1.

**Technical SEO** — The crawlability, speed and structure work that lets a site
be indexed and ranked properly. Module 3.

**Thumbnail** — The still image representing a video, whose job is to earn the
click. Module 8.

**Title tag** — The page title a search engine may use as the clickable headline
in results. Module 3.

**Top of funnel** — The awareness end, where people do not yet know you.
Module 1.

**Traffic source** — Where a visit came from: search, social, email, direct,
referral or paid. Module 11.

### U

**Unique selling proposition (USP)** — The specific reason to choose you rather
than an alternative. Module 18.

**Unsubscribe rate** — The share of recipients who opt out of an email.
Module 9.

**URL** — The address of a single page. Module 2.

**User acquisition** — The reports and work covering how new people first
arrive. Module 11.

**User experience (UX)** — How easy and pleasant something is to use. Module 2.

**UTM parameter** — A tag added to a link so analytics can report which source,
medium and campaign a visit came from. Module 11.

### V

**Value proposition** — What a customer gets, for whom, and why it is better
than the alternative. Module 18.

**Vanity metric** — A number that rises reliably without the business being
better off. Module 1.

**Video SEO** — Optimising a video so it is found through search, on the
platform and off it. Module 8.

**Viewability** — Whether an advert was actually in view, rather than merely
served.

**Voice search** — Searching by speaking rather than typing, which tends to
produce longer, question-shaped queries. Module 16.

### W

**Webhook** — An automated message one system sends another when an event
happens, used to join tools together. Module 17.

**Welcome sequence** — The first few automated emails someone receives after
subscribing. Module 9.

**Word of mouth** — People recommending you to each other. The oldest earned
media there is. Module 1.

**Workflow** — A defined sequence of automated steps with triggers and
conditions. Module 17.

### Z

**Zero-click search** — A search answered on the results page, so no site gets
the visit. The reason AEO and GEO exist. Module 16.

---

## A note on definitions

Where a definition depends on a tool — bounce rate, open rate, engagement rate,
keyword difficulty — the tool decides, and tools disagree. Always check how
yours calculates a number before comparing it with anything.

lessons.title: Templates 1 to 10: strategy, audience and planning
lessons.description: Persona, funnel, segmentation, KPIs, strategy, competitors, SWOT, STP, journey map and campaign brief.
lessons.content:
## How to use these

Thirty templates across three pages. Every one has a **Copy** and a **Download**
button, so you can take it into a document, a spreadsheet or a notes app and
fill it in.

They are deliberately plain text. A template that only works inside one tool
stops working when you change tools.

**Templates 11 to 20** cover SEO, content and social. **Templates 21 to 30**
cover ads, email, analytics and client work.

---

## 1. Buyer persona

Used in module 1. One per distinct buyer, two or three at most.

:::template Template 1 - Buyer persona
PERSONA NAME AND AGE:
Which business this is for:

SITUATION
- Job or life stage:
- The circumstances that matter here:
- Evidence (review / conversation / search data / ASSUMPTION):

GOAL
- What they are trying to achieve:
- What "solved" looks like to them:
- Evidence:

BARRIERS
- What stops them buying:
- What they have been burned by before:
- What they would need to believe to go ahead:
- Evidence:

WHERE THEY ALREADY LOOK
- What they type into a search engine:
- Which platforms, if any:
- Whose opinion they trust:
- Evidence:

SO WHAT
- One thing this changes about the website:
- One thing this changes about the message:
- One channel this rules in or out:
:::

If the SO WHAT box is empty, the persona is decoration.

## 2. Marketing funnel map

:::template Template 2 - Funnel map
Business:
Objective:

AWARENESS      asset:                     measured by:
INTEREST       asset:                     measured by:
CONSIDERATION  asset:                     measured by:
CONVERSION     asset:                     measured by:
RETENTION      asset:                     measured by:
ADVOCACY       asset:                     measured by:

THE GAP
- Stage with no asset:
- What I will build for it:
- Why that addresses the gap rather than adding more traffic:

lessons.title: Cheat sheet: SEO and content tools
lessons.description: What each kind of SEO tool is for, and a workflow that survives the tools changing.
lessons.content:
## Before you use this

> **Everything on this page goes out of date.** Interfaces move, free tiers
> change, features are renamed and removed. This sheet covers what each tool is
> *for* and what to look for inside it. Check the current interface, the current
> terms and the current pricing yourself before you rely on any of it.

Nothing here ranks tools against each other on figures. A ranking built on
prices and limits is wrong within a month.

---

## What each kind of tool is for

```
  WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW              KIND OF TOOL
  --------------------------------   ------------------------------
  Is my site indexed? What do I       Search console provided by the
  already rank for?                   search engine itself
  What do people search for?          Keyword research tool
  What is my site technically          Crawler
  getting wrong?
  Who links to my competitors?         Backlink index
  Is my page fast enough?              Page experience tester
  Is my markup valid?                  Structured data validator
```

Start with the free tools the search engines give you. They are the only source
with your actual data; everything else is an estimate.

## Search console

The search engine's own view of your site. Free.

**What it answers:** which pages are indexed, which queries you appear for, how
often people click, and what is broken.

**Look for:** coverage or indexing reports, the performance or queries report,
the mobile usability report, and the sitemap submission area.

**The one habit worth building:** sort queries by impressions, then look for
ones with many impressions and almost no clicks. Those are pages that rank but
do not earn the click — usually a title problem, which is the cheapest fix in
SEO.

## Keyword research tools

**What they answer:** what people search for, roughly how often, and roughly how
competitive it is.

**Look for:** a keyword ideas view, a "questions" filter, and a way to see which
pages currently rank.

**The trap:** volume and difficulty figures are estimates, calculated differently
by every tool. Never compare a difficulty score from one tool with another, and
never present either as fact to a client.

**The habit:** filter for intent before volume. A lower-volume keyword where the
searcher wants to buy is worth more than a high-volume one where they want a
definition.

## Crawlers

**What they answer:** what a search engine sees when it walks your site —
broken links, duplicate titles, missing descriptions, redirect chains, orphan
pages.

**Look for:** a crawl report grouped by issue type, and an export you can hand
to a developer.

**The habit:** crawl before and after any site change. The before gives you
something to compare against when something breaks.

## Backlink tools

**What they answer:** who links to you, who links to competitors, and what
links you could plausibly earn.

**The trap:** every tool has a different index, so link counts disagree. Use
them to find opportunities, not to report a number.

## Page experience and validators

**What they answer:** how quickly a page becomes usable, and whether your
structured data is valid.

**The habit:** test on a phone profile and a slow connection, not on your own
laptop on office broadband.

## Analytics (for content)

**What it answers:** which content gets found, which keeps people, and which
leads anywhere.

**The habit:** judge content on what it caused, not on page views. A page with
modest traffic that produces leads beats a popular page that produces nothing.

## A workflow that survives tool changes

```
  1  Search console    what am I already close to ranking for?
  2  Keyword tool      what else do these people search?
  3  Intent check      what do they actually want?  look at what ranks now
  4  Crawler           can the page be found and understood?
  5  Write / fix
  6  Validator         is the markup right?
  7  Search console    did impressions and clicks move, 4 to 8 weeks later
```

Four to eight weeks is the honest wait. Anyone promising faster is selling
something.

:::checklist SEO tool starter checklist
- Search console verified for the site
- Sitemap submitted
- Analytics installed and recording
- A crawl run, and its worst five issues written down
- One keyword sheet started, with intent recorded per keyword
- Page experience tested on a phone profile
- Structured data validated on one template page
:::
